OrderEventsConsumer.SubjectFor maps "order.refund-requested", "order.refunded", "order.refund-failed" to email subjects and saves a pending email job. RabbitMQ Exchanges page (topic): keys "are separated into segments by `.`"; `*` matches exactly one segment, so order.* matches order.refund-requested.

DonHang.Api/Messaging/PaymentEventsConsumer.cs:107-109: if (routingKey == "payment.refunded") await orders.CompleteRefundAsync(...); else if (routingKey == "payment.refund-failed") await orders.FailRefundAsync(...); else throw new PoisonMessageException(...). Comment above HandleAsync: "payment.refunded cancels the order and saves an order.refunded outbox row; payment.refund-failed compensates instead, back to `paid`, with an order.refund-failed row."

PaymentEventsConsumer.OnReceivedAsync: catch (PoisonMessageException) { ... await channel.BasicRejectAsync(delivery.DeliveryTag, requeue: false); }. The throw happens before any SaveChangesAsync, so the order is unchanged. RabbitMQ DLX page: messages are dead-lettered when rejected "by an AMQP 0.9.1 consumer using basic.reject or basic.nack with requeue parameter set to false"; orders.payment-events has x-dead-letter-exchange = orders.dead-letter.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed text): the plain-words rewrite drops where the message goes. orders.payment-events is declared with x-dead-letter-exchange (DonHang.Api/Messaging/RabbitMqTopology.cs:43), so BasicRejectAsync(requeue: false) dead-letters the message; it is not simply dropped. "give up on the message" can read as discarded.
issues.quote: turns into telling RabbitMQ to give up on the message instead of delivering it again, so it never changes the order.
